stem.text: Classify the series \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{9 \left(-1\right)^{n} n}{n + 9} \) as absolutely convergent, conditionally convergent, or divergent.

answer_key.label: The series diverges, because its terms do not approach 0.

worked_solution.text: Look at the size of the terms: \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{9 n}{n + 9} = 9 \).
Since the terms of the series do not approach 0, the series diverges by the nth term test, and neither kind of convergence applies.

options.label: The series converges absolutely, because its terms alternate in sign.
options.derivation: absolute values never considered and the alternation taken as enough for convergence, then called absolute

options.label: The series converges conditionally, because its terms alternate in sign while their sizes do not shrink.
options.derivation: the absolute and conditional labels exchanged on an alternating-series reading

options.label: The series diverges, because its terms do not approach 0.
The series converges, because it is an alternating series.
options.derivation: a convergence conclusion drawn without saying which series it concerns
